import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    events = inputs["events"].copy()

    # Sort by user_id, event_ts, event_id
    events = events.sort_values(
        by=["user_id", "event_ts", "event_id"],
        ignore_index=True
    )

    # Extract date (calendar date in server local timezone, assumed to be naive)
    events["event_date"] = events["event_ts"].dt.date

    # Determine new-session flag per row
    prev_user = events["user_id"].shift(1)
    prev_ts = events["event_ts"].shift(1)
    prev_date = events["event_date"].shift(1)

    same_user = events["user_id"] == prev_user
    same_date = events["event_date"] == prev_date

    gap_minutes = (events["event_ts"] - prev_ts).dt.total_seconds() / 60.0

    new_session = (
        (~same_user) |
        (same_user & ~same_date) |
        (same_user & same_date & (gap_minutes > 45))
    )
    # first row overall is always a new session (NaN comparisons -> True via ~same_user)
    new_session.iloc[0] = True

    # Session number resets per user: cumulative count of new_session flags within each user group
    events["_new_session_flag"] = new_session.astype(int)
    events["session_num"] = events.groupby("user_id")["_new_session_flag"].cumsum()

    # Group by user_id and session_num to aggregate
    user_sessions = events.groupby(
        ["user_id", "session_num"],
        as_index=False
    ).agg(
        session_date=("event_date", "first"),
        session_start=("event_ts", "min"),
        session_end=("event_ts", "max"),
        event_count=("event_id", "count")
    )

    # Ensure columns are in the correct order
    user_sessions = user_sessions[
        ["user_id", "session_num", "session_date", "session_start", "session_end", "event_count"]
    ]

    return {"user_sessions": user_sessions}
